title: Physics-Informed Learning for Multiplayer Differential Games
abstract: arXiv:2611.33644v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Computing per-player feedback strategies in $N$-player adversarial differential games is challenging as the associated coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman system is high-dimensional and generally lacks classical solutions. We address this by approximating viscosity solutions using physics-informed neural networks within a policy iteration scheme with a vanishing-viscosity annealing schedule. Theoretically, we establish an explicit $\varepsilon$-Nash guarantee by bounding per-player regret via computable residuals and prove our method reaches this stopping criterion in finite time. For two-player zero-sum games, we further establish a computable bound on the approximation error of the value function. Numerical experiments on pursuit-evasion scenarios illustrate the tightness of these computed bounds and the framework's scalability to high-dimensional environments.

translated_title: 面向多人微分博弈的物理信息学习方法
translated_abstract: 在N人对抗性微分博弈中计算各玩家的反馈策略极具挑战性，因为相关的耦合哈密顿-雅可比-贝尔曼方程组是高维的，且通常缺乏经典解。为解决这一问题，我们在带有消失粘性退火调度的策略迭代框架中，利用物理信息神经网络来逼近粘性解。在理论方面，我们通过可计算的残差对每个玩家的遗憾值进行界定，建立了显式的ε-纳什保证，并证明了该方法能在有限时间内达到此停止准则。对于两人零和博弈，我们进一步给出了价值函数逼近误差的可计算上界。在追逃场景上的数值实验表明了这些计算所得界的紧致性，以及该框架在高维环境中的可扩展性。
tldr: 该论文提出一种在策略迭代框架内结合消失粘性退火调度、利用物理信息神经网络逼近N人对抗性微分博弈粘性解的方法，并通过可计算残差给出了显式的ε-纳什保证及有限时间收敛性证明。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes approximating viscosity solutions of N-player adversarial differential games using physics-informed neural networks within a policy iteration scheme with vanishing-viscosity annealing, establishing explicit ε-Nash guarantees via computable residuals and proving finite-time convergence to the stopping criterion.
